boundaries: A boundary is not a vendor, library, implementation, option review, test result or deployed binding.
A diagram arrow or boundary name alone does not specify the contract, custody or owner; changing its behavioral obligation requires a new version and review.
claim_ceiling: Generated project-scoped candidate Definition record only. Shape and projection checks grant no Lab admission, semantic truth, implementation, collection or employment-use authority.

scope.applicability: One named product capability crossing or replaceable subsystem interface across option and release cycles.
exclusions: Any other product or Lab-wide meaning without separate owner review and admission.

domain_context.explanation: Candidate Integration Boundary meaning for the Engineer Assessment product and research program. Its construct, implementation and use claims remain bounded by the source statement.

plain_language.explanation: The stable seam in the product: what crosses it and what must remain true even if the library or provider changes.

boundary_conditions: A boundary is not a vendor, library, implementation, option review, test result or deployed binding.
A diagram arrow or boundary name alone does not specify the contract, custody or owner; changing its behavioral obligation requires a new version and review.
scientific_formal.normative_statement: An Integration Boundary is a versioned, owner-scoped point where product components, external services or trust zones exchange data or responsibility under a stable behavioral contract. It identifies the producer and consumer, inputs and outputs, data sensitivity and purpose, required invariants, failure and recovery behavior, and the interface that candidate implementations must satisfy independent of vendor choice.
